title: Playing drums in Maurice Durand's band
summary: Gabriel joined Maurice Durand's reading band on drums, lists its members, and recalls Durand's later move to California.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: No, I'm going to tell you, that fellow, when he came here, he was playing with Maurice Durand. You ever heard of Maurice Durand?
Oh, yes, I met him once, down in the 9th Ward on the Duzardi extreme.

Well, I went in that band playing drums too, in that band with Maurice Durand. And Jimbo had left the band, so they took London, Willie Umphrey was playing in the band, Clarence Willie. Yeah. When Willie left, then they took London Vare in the band. London Vare, Buddy Johnson, and Maurice Durand, that was a three-blowing instrument. So, they had Green playing guitar, Green, and I think they had T-Boy on bass. And they had a couple other drums, trying to see somebody else. I know I was playing from the first place. Happy come out that band, Rayd Happy. Oh, yeah.
I never knew anything about him. You heard of him?

He was a good ragtime drummer. Well, I went in that band behind Happy, but I could play on the music, because the band was all reading music and it was just in my hand. I could jazz and play that music. So, the first piece we played, yes, we have no bananas. We have no bananas today. So, I got in that band and I played with that band and it was very nice. We'd get the jobs to go over the lake to play and we'd make on the train. Maurice was pretty straight Maurice Durand, my daddy Chris and his wife. And he was a nice fellow. He had a nice band, but I don't know. He was a fellow for a little while to go down. He wanted to go to New York, because all these men wanted to go to New York. So, I don't know what happened to him. Did he die?
Maurice, he went to California. I saw him, Professor Mineta and I went over there in 1958 and saw him, talk to him. And he died though about three or four years ago.
Yeah, well, Durand, he was a nice trumpet player.
Yeah, he was pretty straight though, I guess.
Yeah, he was straight, just like I said.
From Mineta and other people said. I never did hear him, I did hear him get his horn out and he played a few notes, you know, that's a little warm up.
Yeah, well, he was a nice trumpet player.
Had a nice tone and all. He wasn't playing anymore professionally when I heard.
